tips.comment: Should be able to put debut effort finishing third at Kempton to good use. Stepping up by a furlong may allow him to go close in this ordinary contest.

William Haggas's only runner here has Tom Marquand booked to ride. A pointer of a big run appearing on debut run, with the stable in great form. Earthwatch has been gelded, so he may be a settled horse that can give his running.
Looks a winnable race. Cost 150k in the breeze-ups last year. Was very weak in the market on debut last time, ridden for another day. There is support for him today, so that day could be today.
Bought from top Fabre yard in France and bred in the purple for Godolphin, you have to like the look of Romieu here. Deserves a chance and looks a steal at 18,000 gns.

Has won two from two here at Redcar, over 6f and 5f. Made a decent return from absence last time out when 5th, that's after being hampered. But should be fitter for that outing and back here should go well.
Top booking here for Kranjcar, who keeps flattering to deceive. But this is a long way to come from the Boughey yard and could well be a good thing in this race.

9yo mare Little Muddy has dropped to a more than dangerous mark 17lbs below her last winning mark from May 23. Wasn't disgraced lto over 5f at Doncaster. Drops to class 6 here today and the step up in trip should suit. Shouldn't be far away.

Has run well here over this trip including a close up second place last August. Very good at Newcastle this year with a win, two places and a close up fourth. Trainer had a huge price winner on the Newcastle good friday card. Jockey in brilliant form with six winners in the last two weeks at a strike rate over twenty percent.
Birdie Bowers returns to the turf at Redcar after a spell on the all weather. Even running 1lb out of the handicap, he can reach a place based on his form of 2 years ago.

Tickets has done her best work on the all-weather and her turf form hasn’t quite matched that yet. She’s unproven on quick ground too, but if she can transfer that AW level to turf, she’d be really well treated and could surprise a few.
Outpaced early over 5 furlongs at Nottingham 9 days ago but finished well, going third inside the final half a furlong. This step up in trip will be welcome.
Will probably run his usual honest race, but this is about as good as he is. Good enough to get placed here off 47, but unlikely to get his head in front.
John Kirkup recently returned from a spell on the all-weather. He prefers the turf and can go close off this low mark.

Going for Stroxx to run a big race under Billy Garritty for the Liam Bailey yard. He has won three times now in 63 starts, with two of them coming this year. Nudged up 2lb for winning last time, but could still be involved in the finish again here today.
Showed there is lots of room for improvement LTO when returning to turf at Catterick when 7 of 9 earlier this month. I like he is back down to last winning mark, which just might make the difference.
Not a very deep race and Fast Flo comes all the way from Norfolk to have a pop at this race. Given that and the booking of excellent Jack Callan, has to be worth an each way chance.

Media Mogul can go well for the Ed Walker yard. Media Mogul won last time out in first-time cheekpieces at Wolverhampton. Can go well again in them, and up in trip will be good as well for this horse.

Ribba Hill had to cut out the running in a slowly run race over a mile and 6 furlongs at Southwell last month. He is lightly raced and that was his first run over 14f. He stays this distance and has now dropped five pounds in the weights since January.

Looks quite short in the market for what looks a tight-looking race. But with top jockey Tom Marquand booked to ride, I can see a big run after finishing 4th of 14 to 'Stanage' at Doncaster (7f 6yds) on good ground in a Class 4 Handicap last month. Off a 1lb lower mark back on today's quicker ground, it could be hard to beat.
A three-time course and distance winner, he will benefit from the drop in trip from his promising seasonal return. Not ideally drawn, but David Allan does better than his average here.

Al Muqdad had a very busy campaign last year, racing 19 times. He is turned out fresh here on seasonal return, and this represents a slightly easier level of competition than the 20k handicap he raced in September. He may not need to be fully wound up to be competitive today.
Worth a chance because of how well he goes fresh, including at this track. Has his favored ground, although rain won't bother him and is back on a competitive mark.

Was Superb winning 2nd run here at a shorter distance back in October 2022 but did not show much ability LTO at Newcastle in May of 2023. Has been off for 23 months, but this is the best course to return to, now running off the lowest career mark.
Woodstock comes on leaps and bounds for their first run, and this could be another example of that. Available at a big price, surely an each-way bet here.

7F here might be the perfect track for him if he is able to kick on. He was just caught at Newcastle and Southwell when trying those tactics. It's difficult making up ground here on quick ground, so he could nick the race.

The Green Man has not been great of late, but I would put that down to the going, as he won twice on Good/GF in 2023. However, all runs since last year have been on Soft or AW. I think the return to GF today after wind surgery could spark a revival, now 9 lbs lower than that last win. EW.

Didn't really cut much ice on the AW but bounced back to form on his most recent start when finishing 2nd of 13 to 'Alzahir' at Thirsk (7f) on Good Ground in a Class 4 Handicap earlier this month. Despite going up 3lb for that effort, he still looks very well handicapped on a number of efforts last term.

My play in the feature at Redcar this afternoon comes in the form of BOY DOUGLAS at 9/2. Rhythm Master will do well to overcome G Harker’s 13% SR (A/E0.44) with favourites in 4yo+ races, meanwhile the M Appleby yard have had a torrid AW season (again) and are just 1/28 (A/E 0.29) over the past month. They don’t usually have theirs wound up for the spring so I don’t expect things to pick up quite yet so Grabajabba can be opposed also. Barley could prove to be the fly in the ointment but D Allan has been on the decline for a number of years now and is just 2/38 (A/E 0.49) so far this season. Magna Grecia brings a few negatives for Cadarn to overcome; most notably a 3% SR (A/E 0.3) on straight courses and I can’t make cases for the outsiders so BD looks the obvious choice. The son of New Bay isn’t the most consistent but was 1l runner up on reappearance last season and has only been tried once at this level. NB brings a deluge of positives; most notably a 36% SR (A/E 1.32) with fancied runners coming up in class.
Decent enough record on turf and you can't turn your nose up at this horse's chances here. Has a great each way chance.

Yaaser may need a run or two to come good, but with bottom weight here and Amy Waugh riding with confidence, he can produce a very good run. Jim Goldie's trained seven-year-old is on a fair mark of 70.
Triple Double A had a longer break. His last race was in December last year at Wolverhampton and he was 7th in a field of twelve. But I think he's in good form today. Jockey is still Jason Hart.

Flamborough Head looked to have something left in the tank when winning comfortably over C&D last time, finishing with ears pricked and doing it nicely. Up 5lb but with a top trainer at the track and more likely to come, he’s got a strong chance of going in again.
Ottoman changed yards this month and came straight in with a win when stepping up to 1 mile. He drops another 1 lb, and I would expect more improvement now second up.

MWAFAQ looks very interesting on handicap debut here for Richard Fahey. Three races to get his mark of 60 and now stepping up in trip from 5f to 1m for the first time. That suggests to me he's been running over inadequate trips and the horse will suddenly improve for the step up in trip and that will be the reason the trainer gives. Potential handicap plot for me.

Plenty having their first run in a handicap today, and that could throw up an unexpected result. Hurricane Bea's qualifying race was a relatively high-value novice stakes with £14k in prize money. The 37k gelding steps up to a mile now, and it is not impossible that will bring out some improvement off a bargain basement mark of 51 (jockey claims a further 5).

Perfidia was unlucky not to get her head in front at Pontefract and she’s been knocking on the door for a while now. She’s with a trainer who does well at Redcar and looks set to be right in the mix again in a race like this.

This horse has not been settling in her races, but this is just her 6th start. She makes her debut for a new stable here today, and hopefully, that will be the key to seeing the horse's true potential. Her sire produces some nice types that do well on good ground, and her new trainers not only have a terrific strike rate this year, but they have also had 5 winners at the course in the last year from just 12 entries. David Nolan takes over in the saddle, and he's been doing well for the yard too, so there are enough new variables here to suspect we may well see a lot more from the horse now.

An open-looking sprint where a chance is taken on 20/1 shot Hardlass. Her form is a bit in and out, but if she repeats her run at Wolverhampton a couple of runs back, she should be bang there. Her handicap mark has dropped to a winnable-looking mark.

Arias Dream showed potential on her penultimate race when a close second in October. She was a beaten favourite next time and from the explanation offered to the stewards, one might infer the filly was still weak and immature. Connections are fitting a hood today which might signal a better run.
Super selection. The top-rated horse on the Darth Niloc Ratings. Yard inform and good jockey onboard. Maximum stakes advised. Best bet of the day.

Moon Over The Sea was well backed and got the job done over this C&D two starts back, then ran respectably enough last time. Dropping back in trip looks a plus and with his course form holding up, he’s got fair claims of getting involved again.

Good record at the track with a win and three seconds this year alone. Overall race record is one win and six places, and this looks like a good opportunity. Consistency alone suggests that he is well up to winning off this mark. Holding the market position and worth a bet at this price.

Open looking race, many with chances and Sea Of Charm appears as one with a chance. Ran well in defeat over 1m2f at Lingfield last time on what was her first run back from a rest , now steps back up in tip, she has shown her best form over this distance of 1m4f and it's encouraging that she does have good form in the book at this course so although today's wide draw isn't ideal, she can still be considered as it is possible to run well over this course and distance from this wide draw.

Walk The Moon can go well for the Carroll yard. Walk The Moon has been placed in 5 of his 20 race starts and has the low weight today in this handicap. Ran okay over track and trip last time out and can do better.

This horse looked to be a bit ahead of the handicapper when winning for this jockey just 2 starts ago and looks great value at 20/1 off just a 3lb higher mark. He clearly acts well around here and appears to have been completely overlooked in the market. The jockey has some great stats for a 5lb apprentice too so there's a lot of positives for such a big outsider.

Four time course and distance winner who was last seen over this course and distance 34 day's ago where finishing 7th/9 where off to a messy hampered start in a race that was not run to suit Pysanka's nature of going on the occasion however D M Loughnane's inmate is no horse to overlook over this course this course and distance and he is more than capable of bouncing back here in a race that should be run suit with his favoured gallop at his disposal this time out given the horses enrolled to run here currently operating on a very attractive mark of 58 Pysanka looks poised to strike here and worth noting he is now operating 2lb below his last winning mark jockey Edward Greatrex takes the ride and can give Pysanka a promising ride here at Wolverhampton price at the time sof writing looks of very good E/W value must be taken seriously and accordingly

Synergism hasn’t shown much in three runs so far but typical of a Prescott type, he’s likely been brought along with handicaps in mind. Up in trip and slowly away last time, there’s a fair chance he improves now tackling this new distance. Market support says he’s expected to figure.
The step up in trip over C&D looked to do the trick, taking its first win. Looks dangerous at the mark still, especially over a trip and course where it found its first success.

Legacy Power didn’t fire last time after a long layoff but had some solid C&D form last season. With that run under his belt and a strong trainer-jockey combo in his corner, he’s a contender if bouncing back to anything like his best.
Won at this course on debut and has been running well lately. Caught further back than ideal behind Psychodrama last time and is two pounds better off so can reverse that form here. Forecast 4/1.
Big price with 7 lb being taken off to go 1 lb above last winning mark. Solid form over CD and could go close today.

Reigning Profit just missed out at Pontefract last time and looks to have hit a consistent level again. Conditions are ideal, the yard took this race last year and he looks a solid threat if running to that same mark.

Solid CD record, being in the frame 4 from 5 in the last 6 months. Ran to good figures when in the first 3 and can see another strong run today. 3lb above last winning mark but has the best course form against today's rivals.

Recon Mission looks a solid each-way play from the plum draw on a track where early speed counts. He had a dead heat win against Midnightattheoasis, who races in this today and with the same weight swing. It will be difficult to overcome today's favorite, but if he gets caught up in midfield, then Recon Mission could very well come close.
Worth an each-way punt as he has won 4 times previously around here. Comes here looking to follow up after winning last time. Won on turf from a 2 lb higher mark a year ago, so won't be far away.
Very reliable type and goes well at this course. A previous C/D winner as well, looks a well-worthy favorite for this race and is ideally drawn to strike once again.

Broke her duck at the 15th time of asking when striking at Southwell last month and promptly followed up at Newcastle. Arguably career best when 2nd beaten a neck last time and is clearly thriving at present so should go very well once again.

In good form, currently winning an amateur riders' race here and then running with credit at Thirsk. Niven has a cracking strike rate here, and the good conditional coming on board is an obvious improvement on the amateur last time out here. Overpriced currently at 9s.

American Star has struggled for form lately and didn’t show much at Catterick last time, but he’s now on a very tempting mark and does go well on Tapeta. Trip suits and if the drop in weight sparks a revival, he could outrun his odds.
Outreach has had all of his three wins here, with the latest being in February off a 45. Last year, he won here off a 48, which makes me think he is worth an EW 4P chance today.
Luke Morris on board with another runner with strong CD form. 3lb above last winning mark but ultra consistent and can see a step up to take the win here again.
Form has dipped again unfortunately, but the last 12 runs have been here. It is also a 5-time course winner and 1lb below the last winning mark. The price is a little overpriced in my opinion.

I've a strong suspicion that the canny trainer, who often lines up their horses off competitive handicap marks, might have done just that here and booked a jockey that's won 3 of his last 7 rides for the stable. If you look at the horse's 4th of 11 in her only race at this track, then it's easy to make a case that she's well in here off 50 since she was in and around horses rated in excess of 10 lb higher. So she could well be worth siding with, having been lowered 8 lb since her opening handicap mark and returning to the track for the first time since that 4th place finish.

Mark Loughnane's dual C&D winner City Escape didn't put up her best performance when finishing fourth here in a seller behind Danehill Star two weeks ago. She meets the winner again this evening on six lbs better terms, and looks capable of bouncing back to land her third C&D win of the year.

Morris takes the mount again with the selection looking overpriced. Consistent over CD last 6 months and recording some good figures still in defeat. More than happy to take a good price on a consistent CD type.
Pragnell ran well in second here back in February in what looks like a very good race. That was over an extended trip, and back over this distance, can get the win.

I really like this horse today. Finished runner-up in 2 points and started over hurdles over course and distance last time in a useful 3 runner. He probably would have finished 2nd and in front of the 1-2 fav Newton Tornado, who has won since but made a mistake at the last. So more can be expected this time with plenty in his favor.

The horse in third behind Pragnell won a class 5 handicap next time off a mark of 105, which boosts his form. But Deep Purple was in the frame with Wendigo, a runner-up in a Grade 1 next time, and Lightingupourday, who won a class 4 emphatically off a mark of 112. Deep Purple's form looks much stronger, and although he has been off the track for 165 days, you get the feeling Skelton will have him fit enough for this drop in grade.

Zaochen Enki looked much sharper second time out when winning nicely at Wincanton and with the yard having a great record in this race, there’s every chance he steps forward again. Looks a big threat and should be right in the mix.

Paul Nicholls' Zaochen Enki is a standout in this race, having been a ready winner at Wincanton on UK debut. There is no reason not to support him and also have an each-way saver given the shape of the market. Golden Echo appeals; she is a mare by the up-and-coming jumps stallion Golden Horn. A winner on the flat, she ran okay on hurdles debut after a layoff. If building on that, she might bag a place in receipt of 7 pounds mares' allowance.

ANOTHER LIFETIME is an interesting runner making hurdles debut. A four year old who runs for a top northern yard and there was something to like about his recent run when competing on the level. With an experienced pilot aboard he needs a market check.

Completed hat trick during the winter and was beaten odds-on favorite on penultimate outing but still went well in 2nd. Made a mistake last time out and hung right after but finished 2nd. Should go well again here and with not much in the way of dangers, should win it. Drop back in trip will suit.

Idealko's class ceiling appears to be below this grade of race, and he might be vulnerable today. Sao Carlos, on the other hand, should be competitive at this level and has come a long way down in the weights in twelve months. If settling in the preliminaries today, his early blunder last time can be forgiven.
Gower Prince from Matt Sheppard's stable, whose horses are running well, has Stan Sheppard in the plate. He could be producing him with a telling run for a result appearing.

A veteran these days and has had his problems over the last 18 months. Another new trainer and something to prove today. If he's fit and run somewhere close to his form of a couple of years ago then he could actually win this. Very fairly treated.
Saint Segal sets the standard off of his win in the winter at Newbury. He has run well in handicaps since then without winning but comes here with a real chance.
Won here in April last year from 3lbs lower and is at the foot of the weights here fresher than most. Ran well here first up this season in a class 3 handicap when 3rd from 1lb higher.

Dual winner over hurdles and gained 2nd chase victory when scoring at Wincanton in November. Raised 4 lbs for that , but ran up a hat-trick of runner-up finishes in valuable handicaps , befort finishing a credible 4th in the Greatwood Gold Cup at Newbury last month. Not so good last time, but has dropped to a nice mark.

It is difficult to oppose the consistent Saint Segal, but he has gone a long way up in the weights and has been beaten off marks in the high 130s three times now. Whereas Bourbali is well-handicapped and is also a course and distance winner with good ground being no issue.

Western General has won his last two starts and three out of five this season. He won by 7 lengths at Newton Abbot in October and bounced back from two defeats to win by a combined margin of 32 lengths in his last two starts at Wincanton and Hereford. He is up another 10 lbs, but in his current form, he has a great chance of winning again.
Twice a course and distance winner and should be much more at home over this track and trip after racing over further at Aintree last time out when a respectable 6th in a field of 30 in the Topham.

The interestingly sponsored Tip Top Lavish Latrine Handicap Hurdle is a tricky event. Speiriuil seems to like the trip but could be better at a furlong shorter. Lorcan Murtagh has ridden him in the last 10 of 11 races that he has run, with one victory to his name. Nigel Hawke regularly has runners at Chepstow with a mild degree of success. Easter Monday is often a day to keep your money in your sky for punting purposes, though of course, the winners are always there. Raised nine pounds, I think, since its last victory, which is a bit harsh. I feel one for a mild each way rather than all of your cash plus 3 buttons type of bet (always bet within your means).

Hopefully, the ground here has remained fairly good as she has shown her best form on a sound surface. She ran well in a Class 1 last time. She drops to Class 4 here, having won twice last spring. Looks worth chancing each way here with 4 places available.

Geezer Rockstar ran his best race on good ground in a Class 3 maiden at Ascot last March. Four races since in better class or on softer ground have not been inspiring, but he has dropped 8 lb in the weights and is dropped to a Class 4 event today for return from 6 months off following wind surgery. The win at Ascot came after 83 days off. With the yard in form, he could be fully wound up and has big claims in this if that's the case.

The Magus was nicely backed from 100/1 into 16s last time when making the frame on a handicap qualifier. That was an encouraging run, and the handicapper has awarded him a mark of just 100. With only 10-13 today, the five-year-old could show further improvement.

Bertie B opened up this term with a second, followed by a C4 win at 2m4f by over 3L. But took on weight, stepped up in trip and class to C3. I think today's drop to 2m3f and C4 might see a revival EW 4P.
This one showed quite well last time over the jumps, finishing 6th, beaten after a mistake. Perhaps things happened a little fast for him. Upped in trip, he can do better EW.
Ri Na Cuirte ran a blinder in second last time out, only getting beaten by a favorite who he battled hard. If he runs to the same standard, he can go close here. 5 places each way for money back.

QUITE THE GETAWAY is a mare who has been withdrawn from recent races holding multiple entries and that may have been with half an eye on this contest. Her latest promising effort signalled she may now have come to hand and this slightly more extreme test of stamina should suit. Proven on ground this quick she appeals.

Sawpit Samantha got this trip well when tried over it for the first time last time, finishing well to take 3rd. The long run in at this track will give her time to get going and she showed on that run 4 weeks ago that she picks up well on good ground. Worsley claims 3lb which offsets the 1lb out the handicap, so she is better off this time than last. Should be able to make her presence felt with a late run today.

My Louise has been gradually improving this season and her RPR of 98 hints that a breakthrough may be near. She carries a handy weight and should appreciate this extended trip. With Marc Goldstein on board, who knows her well, she looks capable of mounting a strong challenge in a wide-open race.

Gorcombe Moonshine has been running consistently well, and his RPR of 102 puts him among the top-rated in the field. He finishes strongly and this trip suits him perfectly. With Harry Kimber taking the reins and conditions to his liking, he’s a major player if things fall into place.

There was enough encouragement to be taken from her fifth-placed stable bow over an inadequate 2m at Stratford 23 days ago to suggest that a race of this nature is within her compass. I wouldn't read too much into her previous point-to-point exploits as she is tiny and reverting to today's 3m distance is sure to see the daughter of Getaway in a better light. Matt Sheppard is enjoying his best ever season and, although it's entirely possible she is too useless to ever win, I'm hopeful that we will see her true ability.
Edward Sexton has boosted the form of Old Park Star's Kempton race by winning next time out. Paul Nicholls eases him a grade today and there is no reason why the 120k gelding cannot run well today.
Unplaced last time out but has strong claims of improvement, this time he's running a bit lighter in weight so could benefit very well.

The model I run suggests Gwennie May Star can win this race ahead of La Dolce Dolly in second and All Authorized in third. This result has largely been driven by Gwennie May Star having the highest RPR of the field but the second lowest OR. This results in less weight being carried over the 3m round trip. This does represent a step up in class today, but Tristan Durrell is on board and claims 3 lbs, which can be the difference by the finish line.

Warranty comes into this in solid form with two recent placed efforts and looks suited to this kind of trip. His latest RPR of 124 puts him right in the mix here, and he’s a previous course winner. Carrying a fair weight and partnered with Freddie Mitchell, he has every chance of landing this.
La Dolce Dolly has scored twice in the last six weeks over the trip and is only 8lbs higher. This race is far from easy but this mare seems to be firing on all cylinders at the moment.
Press Your Luck has saved his best form for Wincanton. This is his first visit to Plumpton, and he is weighted to win if the track conditions suit.

Cracking race this with a case to be made for most of them, but this lad could be a group horse in the handicap (although weighted accordingly). A winner here in the past, and the trainer and jockey have done well here for years. He needs to be faultless, having thrown away his chance at the festival with a bad error 2 out, but if he is, he should have too much for these. Full disclosure - I am also backing Teddy Blue in this race, who also needs a better round of jumping than last time out but is off a belting low weight. He won here for the Moores over hurdles, and the yard and jockey are electric currently.

There is an air of quiet confidence about the current demeanour of Dan Skelton, maybe he knows something we don't. He has clearly marshalled his troops with a view to a big push at the end of the season and so far he has kept his nose in front of Willie Mullins in the trainer's championship. This one looks a likely contributor, being a young improver that has the knack of winning. Eased down winner latest and looks sure to run well again.

Runs over fences for the first time 16 months. Running off a mark of 130. With the jockey taking off a further 5lbs with his claim. Putting him in here off clear bottom weight. He's still lightly raced over fences. Just 5 runs to date. He won first time up. Beating Jetoile quite comfortably. Slowing into the last fence cost him momentum, but he still saved enough to fend off the runner up. He bumped into one in the Grade 2 Wayward Lad Novices. Beaten just a narrow margin by the winner Boothill. Pulling miles clear of the 3rd horse. He put in 2 lesser runs after that. So went back hurdling. His most recent run hinted at a return to form. Bumping into a well handicapped horse in Manuelito. No disgrace there giving him chunks of weight. He boasts 2 wins and 3 places from 6 runs at this track. A solid run looks likely here.

Has been keeping good company and improving my Ed fences backed up by two good seconds on last two starts. Beaten by Special Cadeau the time before last in a Beginners Chase and that one was thought good enough to tackle Grade 1 company at Aintree next time out. Good ground seemed to suit there too and should relish conditions today. Second to Aspire Tower last time reads well too and though looks on a stiff enough mark must be rated highly enough at home to tackle this company on raid to Sussex. Is probably fresher than most too and must have a big chance.

Talented horse that would be dangerous to write off, racing off bottom weight. Has kicked on from chasing debut to win next 2 starts followed up by runner up on last run. Steps up to class 2 company but has top speed rating in the field and has won at this level as a hurdler.

Interesting race this - last display with Cobden on board was highly impressive, and if replicating anything like this performance, will take all the beating here. Raised 9lb for this, but jockey claims 5 back. Back in C2 company, and if he can get up to contest pace early on, will be right there at the line.
Fringill Dike is prone to the odd mistake but likes to run prominently and Plumpton should suit his running style and the better going is in his favour.

Completed an impressive 5-timer when winning at Ascot in November 2024 and raced off 151 in the Desert Orchid at Kempton on the 27th of December when third and a beaten favourite. Not shown much in 3 subsequent showings but off higher marks, now back down to a more realistic mark of 144 here and could go well at a decent price.

This is a very modest Class 3 maiden hurdle and looks a great chance for the consistent Norn Iron, who was just touched off in a hot handicap last time out. Even dropping back in trip should not cause a problem against these rivals.

ROMAN ROY has been placed in two races from six starts. Sixth in a hurdle race over 2m 4f at Plumpton on his latest outing last month. Dropped in trip to 2m should suit and could well be able to win this race.
Pulled up on handicap debut on penultimate start. Surely something was amiss that day as he won his novice race under a penalty last time and should be there or thereabouts.

Latest win at Exeter reads well with the second not disgraced in the Imperial Cup and the third a close second in an Aintree handicap. The extra two furlongs will help on this tighter track. The ground suits, and a prominent style is regularly the way to be around here.
Wicked Thoughts made all to win at Ascot. If he could hold that kind of form with a similar ride from Harry Cobden, he won't be far away.
Mostly Sunny had a couple of wins in June and the handicapper judged him harshly for that. His mark has slowly reduced since then and a much improved performance is expected today.
Lady Jago absolutely bolted up last week and looks good to bring up a hat trick here. Her win two races ago at Wincanton has been cranked by one of the ones behind winning at Cheltenham last week.
Sea Invasion is a strong bet to win. This one has been running well lately, and this looks entirely winnable for him. Strong form and the yard is going well.

Lyrical Genius is an 8-year-old gelding trained by the very underrated Sarah Humphrey. She has 41 wins out of 278 in recent years and seems to have her yard in fine fettle, sending out two winners in recent days in the shape of Flamenco at 9-1 and The Wise Traveller at 9-2. Lyrical Genius made a breakthrough win as a chaser last time out and has been raised 3lb to a mark of 103, but this mark should be well within his grasp, having posted a career-high RPR of 122. Tom Cannon rides, a Plumpton specialist, having picked up 96 winners since 2012. He has ridden 9 times for Sarah Humphrey and won on 3, boasting a 100% win record at Plumpton on a Sarah Humphrey horse, winning on Milan Bridge at 8-1 and Flamenco at 9-1 just yesterday. Connections could be lining another one up here today!

Won a maiden comfortably over course and distance on 2nd UK start. Rex Dingle is an underrated jockey and won 2 starts ago at Newton Abbot. Public Enemy makes handicap debut near the foot of the weights and gets a 4-year-old weight allowance for this contest. Still good value for favourite at 4/1.
A course and distance winner that hasn't won for a while but came back into form last time when second at Sedgefield last month. Looks on a nice handicap mark here.

I'm sure this horse is better than he has shown so far for top connections. It's interesting he qualified on 3 useful maiden runs but disappointed on handicap debut. He was free, and it was on soft, and he won in France on good going. So the better going today after wind surgery could be right up his street, and Nicholls and Cobden will conjure a win out of him before long.

Moonshine Man has been consistent and boasts a decent RPR of 114, giving him a strong chance against similar rivals. He looks capable of further improvement and Brendan Powell is a positive jockey booking. If he brings his A-game, he’s well equipped to fight for top honours in this competitive handicap.
Tends to be a bit in and out, but if he is on song, then he has a decent each-way chance with the jockey taking off 7 lbs, putting him on a net 103, which is what he won off on his penultimate start.

Emerald Poet comes here on debut for Willie Mullins, who is scrapping for every bit of prize money on offer. Must fancy chances with this one and teams up with Cobden again after a couple of big wins together recently.

All eyes are on the Mullins and Skelton runners, and Harry Derham's Emerald Lad may be under the radar. Emerald Lad is sired by Diamond Boy, and with the stable capable of doing well in these National Hunt flat races, we could see Paul O'Brien outdoing Harry Cobden on Willie Mullins' Emerald Poet and Harry Skelton's mount Le Beau Madrik for first place prize money.

The model I run suggests Rio Du Risk can win this one ahead of Emerald Poet and Le Beau Madrik. Rio Du Risk is the youngest horse here without too much experience, but comes here after a good first at Fontwell in a class 5 National Hunt flat. The model shows Rio Du Risk being unexposed, carrying the second lowest weight of the field, and having the highest RPR. This is a large step up in class to a National Hunt flat class 2, but interesting to see how it goes.

He has won in this class before, with 5 career wins across varied ground and distances. Comes off a convincing win last time out at Hereford, and handles good ground and goes well in a tongue strap. Both trainer and jockey are in good form.

Stormin Crossgales didn’t jump great last time but still stuck on for third and might be better judged on earlier efforts. He likes to get on with things and if he's allowed to lead off this lower mark, he could bounce right back into form.
Two-time flat winner Dambuster made a promising hurdles debut when a clear of the rest 2nd to a 1/5F three weeks ago.
Auntie Maggie looks a solid option here to win this one and justify favouritism. She has been running very well lately and can make her class felt here.
Milajess brings solid experience, placing multiple times at this distance, and on similar going. Her 50% strike rate in current headgear suggests she's well equipped today.

Sawpit Sienna appeals in this Class 5 contest at Fakenham due to the price and the 3 places on offer with Bet365. I'm sure Auntie Maggie (current favourite) is the danger. Milajess could go well but has a lot of extra weight from her last race/win. First-time visor could spark a bit more improvement with Sawpit Sienna from her already good run last time out at Ludlow.
Has shown enough in his handicaps so far to suggest this is winnable. Close up 2nd last twice and with not much to beat here, should take advantage and finally get off the mark.
Drops back to a more suitable trip after two tries at 3m, and now 12lb below her last winning mark. Proven in softer ground and with rain on the way, she looks a player if conditions ease.

2 of his 3 wins have come at this track and he has placed in the top 3 in 3 of his last 4 starts so he is in good form. He is still 6lbs higher than his last win here in April, but he will relish these conditions and should win.

The Jamie Snowden-trained Jack N Jones was a fine 2nd on her bumper debut two weeks ago. That looks the best on offer here, and providing this doesn't come too soon, then she should take all the beating here. Gavin Sheehan rides, and he could burn them all off if getting an uncontested lead on this sharp track.

Each way 5/2. What a pimple! Ran a decent third first time up to Gladius, trained by Andrew B, who runs Anzac Day. Looking as if the race would improve him no end. Godolphin run a 900 thousand guineas purchase (sandwich money for them), and Simon Crisford runs one with Derby and Dante entries, plus a batch of very decent possibles. So no mugs race. Ernst is a Frankel horse, as is the Godolphin horse who Buick rides. An interesting event with a view to the turf season in prospect.

Having cost 900,000 gns, Charlie Appleby's charge makes appeal on paper, being a gelding by Frankel out of smart 10f winner Poplin (by Medicean), as well as a half-brother to Persian Royal, very useful over a mile.

Anzac Day looked well above average when bolting up at Newmarket and although he’s been off a while, he’s with a top team who know how to get them ready. He’s giving weight but has the class to handle it if back anywhere near right and could take a bit of beating.
This horse looked like a nice horse the first time out, and I suspect it will be slightly better than a class 5 horse. So, I'm going to take a chance each way.
One of the more expensive debutants in this race at 170k euros and is a sibling to two regular winners, including a Group 1 successor.

Worth an each-way bet. Off since December, but this will be just his third run. Just failed on debut before disappointing last time seen in December, having been weak in the market. Bits and pieces for him this morning.

Lovely progressive horse this one who finished 2nd on debut at Wolverhampton before winning next time out by over 4 lengths here at Kempton, he then won again (albeit only a two runner race) before winning once again to make it three in a row at Salisbury by nearly 5 lengths. Was then put away for nearly 6 months and returned to Kempton when 2nd to Dubai Honour in a Class 1 before most recently winning a Group 3 at Sandown. Been off since (a year) but evidently goes well fresh and enjoys it at Kempton so should take all the beating if ready to go.

Botanical returned from a break last month at 1 mile for his second attempt in listed company after wind surgery and was third. He has in the past run well to second here a couple of times. I think that now, second up after a break and wind surgery, and returning to 1m2f, a trip he did well at before the break, could work.
Whilst a couple of points behind the fav on official ratings, this Frankel gelding has the best of the time figures and the stable has burst into form over the last few days.

Lions Pride can go well for the Gosden yard. Lions Pride was beaten in this race last year, but this trainer is in good form. Lions Pride goes well at Kempton and has won in 2 of 4 starts at this track.

Teumessias Fox really enjoys it at Kempton and won nicely here over a bit further last time. The shorter trip might not be perfect but he’s in good form and knows how to win at this track. If a few of the others don’t fire, he could definitely be right there.

EXOPLANET runs for a yard who do well with runners recruited from elsewhere. This five year old has a long absence to overcome , but the yard can get one ready and it is interesting that he returns in such decent company. The market could help us.

Sky Safari has strong previous form, thrives over a mile, and benefits from Daniel Muscutt’s consistency. Drawn well and proven in similar class, the gelding has pace to dominate and should stay on powerfully. Top rating backed by previous form and jockey-trainer synergy.
Running a hot class one listed fillies on reappearance, and now should Strip fit with that run down 3 classes you can go well, bit of money come for it too

Top Of The Class has to be my pick as she has only had three wins, but they have all been here, with the latest win being in February. While not so good on the step up to C4 last time, I think she can bounce back on the return here with Billy back in the saddle, who was on top for that last win.
The handicapper has given Twirler a chance here to spring a surprise. She is weighted to match her 3rd at Southwell provided her new trainer has her ready after a long break.

Ran a cracker over course and distance last September, just headed in the final 100 yards, with both first and third winning since. Comes here from the same mark with blinkers reapplied and debuts for Boughey, having needed his reappearance run last time when the blinkers were left off.

Was fancied first up @Doncaster LTO but shaped like he would improve for the run. Won a Newmarket handicap from this mark last season and has plenty of positive runs here including a novice stakes win over this trip.

Top weight and the challenges that that brings, but she won last season here first time out. She has run with great credit in both runs at a higher class than this. The yard is running at a 30% strike rate over the last 30 days and a rate of over 20% with seasonal returners. Watson is in cracking form and has improved hugely since leaving Roger Charlton. Well drawn in 3. If she has progressed over the winter from 3 to 4, she should be too good for these.

Metaverse carries a poor FlatStats rating here and Starspangledbanner’s awful 3% SR (A/E 0.3) with runners trained in the south makes his son easy to oppose. Next up SUPREME KING makes the most appeal against at 9/2; the gelding trained by P Evans has been in solid form all winter, accumulating a couple of wins (one over 6f here at Kempton) and a couple of places from six starts. This is a step up in class and trip off the highest rating he’s had for a couple of years, but the son of Kingman has been finishing his races off strongly enough to suggest that he’ll handle it. R Ryan’s 32% SR (A/E 1.26) on fancied 5yo’s is another reason for optimism.
I cannot believe this horse is still a maiden and is definitely reaching a mark where it can be competitive. So it's worth a chance e/w today.

Mark Loughnane's four-time C&D winner Follow Your Heart won by a length at Wolverhampton last month and might have been worth more than the winning margin suggests. With William Buick booked, he could get his fifth win here today. Although he has drifted in the morning market from 13/2 out to nearly double that price, which is a bit worrying.

Kitato Kich steps up to class 3 company for the first time but only has to carry 9 stone for this contest. Neil Callan has been the jockey aboard the last 3 wins, and one of those bits of form ahead of Bint Havana Gold was boosted when winning 3 days ago. Looks good each way value at double figure odds.
Invincible Aura won on the return in January and has been third in three of the four runs this year. That included a C3 and could be thereabouts again while still on an 81. EW

Tiger Crusade's form has dipped the last twice, but with the yard having had a couple of big-priced winners in the last few days (2 winners from the last 5 runners), a chance is taken that he can bounce back. He has 1 win and 2 places from 4 races over C&D, including a head 2nd in a Class 4 handicap from the same mark (85) three starts back. Reunited with Calum Shephard, who has won on him 4 times, he can outrun his odds.

NIBRAS ANGEL is a mare who has been pitched into deeper companyt than she faces here and she makes her debut for a new yard which can help revive. This yard has a decent record with switchers and maybe the market can point us in the right direction with her.

Dream Of Mischief didn’t finish off the season too strongly and now drops to 6f, a trip he hasn’t tackled since his debut. All his wins have come over further, so this could be a sharpener, but he’s got a touch of class and might still run a race if things fall right.
5 from 9 on the AW and 1 from 2 over course & distance. Goes well fresh and is only 3lb higher than for the last win. Yard had a winner recently.
The 6yo is in good form, two near misses and a win in his three runs since Jan. Good RPR ratings, still on a decent mark and the jockey’s 7lb claim should help his chances today.

My vote here goes to one of the two course and distance winners in the field that being Dashing Harry who was last seen at Yarmouth 16 day's ago where finishing 5th/7 however he is more than capable of bouncing back now returning to a polytrack surface and he is more effective on this surface Dashing Harry is the type of horse that needs everything to drop right and good analysis of this class 4 handicap clearly shows Dashing Harry will be well suited in a race of this nature given the horses enrolled to run here currently operating on a mark of 72 he looks poised to strike here and worth noting he is now operating 2lb below his last winning mark jockey A J Farragher takes the ride on James Horton's gelded son Harry Angel and can give this a good shot price at the time if writing looks of decent E/W value must be considered

Hoodie Hoo stepped up nicely from his 2yo debut to win at Wolverhampton and was well backed to do so. He’s clearly going the right way and looks the one to beat among those with experience. Should have more to come.

Not much between Hoodie Hoo and Palmarian on my ratings. Palmarian has a very nice pedigree and I suspect she was nowhere near ready on seasonal return at Doncaster to do herself justice. A much better run is expected today in first time hood.

This Cotai Glory gelding is a half-brother to 3 successful racehorses, including the 6f/7f Victor Taj Neom and the 5.7f winner Kandoo, who achieved this at 2 years old. As a debutant, he is under the guidance of trainer Richard Spencer, who has an impressive track record with first-time runners. Jockey Hollie Doyle, whose remarkable 26% win rate is a testament to her skill, will be in the saddle. At odds of 40/1, it presents a solid each-way opportunity.
Won over the distance in France last year in heavy ground conditions. Today should suit. Was sold for 60,000 guineas after that run. Could be anything.
Rather unexposed on the flat and back down significantly in grade again for this run. Performs well at 2m trip, and Rossa Ryan is a good sign as a confident booking.

Carries top weight today. However, I can't see Cinnodin out of the first 3 here, winning off a 1lb higher before. Still a workable mark and should go well over CD here, of which shown good form previously.

Legacy Power didn’t fire last time after a long layoff but had some solid C&D form last season. With that run under his belt and a strong trainer-jockey combo in his corner, he’s a contender if bouncing back to anything like his best.

MOEL ARTHUR was sent off as favourite the run before last in a grade higher on the poly at Lingfield. So it's quite surprising to see him so readily dismissed after trouble in running on that day, and then a run on tapeta at Southwell last time out, which doesn't seem to suit. Jockey Callum Shepherd won on board him at Lingfield from 2 lbs lower in the weights as recently as January, and there have been some competitive runs at Kempton from a higher handicap mark in the recent past too.

One of four course and distance winners in the race, Legacy Power will again try to go pillar to post, only to set the race up for a finisher. Grey Fox, winner last time out after five months away, can go in again.

Probably has some vibes not to be trusted, not helped by a barren run as it's now been 12 runs since the last win back in 2023. But finished 2 of 4 LTO at Southwell last month and is helped by a drop down in class and can win off the current mark.

Blenheim Lad was a touch disappointing as favourite at Southwell but had been in good form before that, especially over staying trips. Back up in distance here which should suit, and while he’s unproven on Polytrack, the trainer and jockey have a strong record together.

Trinity College is a 3-year-old son of Dubawi ex Hermosa, who herself is a dual 1,000 Guineas winner and from the family of Hydrangea by Galileo. He runs here in this Listed race over 1m2f off a mark of 105. He won his 1m maiden at 10/11f at Galway by 12 lengths last September. Last time out, he won his 1m race at 10/11f at Naas in March. He'll now be ridden by R.L. Moore for Aidan O'Brien and Coolmore. Drawn 4/7 here, I think if he can break and make the rails position, he can make all for some Black Type.

Has won five times in this grade, so has been astutely placed. Top rider Hollie Doyle in the pigskin, and she has won on him twice from three rides. Four wins in these underfoot conditions and is a course and distance winner too. Fresh record not that flash, but maybe he can turn it around this time?

Super Citizen franked some very consistent lead-up form by winning stoutly last time out, and a repeat looks on the cards with B Hughes in the saddle for a very good yard. Course and distance winner, so that augurs well. Ready to go on with it now.

Magic Seven was wisely put aside after failing miserably at Cheltenham in December and resumes here off the back of a 190-day spell. Won first-up in 2023 and it's not beyond the realms of possibility he could repeat that here with the same jockey.
